solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pseudoscience with grand study of corporations

definitions.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, so this is study of the stomach

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for grand, a thousand
astrology, reading fate in the stars, is the classic pseudoscience

explanation.surface: A sneer at some grand academic discipline that analyses big companies, dismissed as no better than quackery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporations' looks like big business, but in old British slang a corporation is a large paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The stomach is the belly, and a corporation is a humorous term for a fat belly, so its study is gastric medicine.

clue.text: Perhaps flat hook with handle

definitions.meaning: in British slang a ... is one's home, a flat being one example
a fishing ... is a barbed hook on a pole for landing fish

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a dwelling, of which a flat is an instance, and also the name of a long-handled fisherman's hook.

clue.text: Sacked lecturer lusts at very strong material

indicators.note: a city that is sacked is ransacked and thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dismissed lecturer lusts after a tough building product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' reads as fired, but it signals the anagram of LECTURER LUSTS AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel shaped into girders and beams for building frames is prized for its great strength.

clue.text: Republican base harbouring single unknown source of shooting?

indicators.note: a place harbouring something holds it within, so the base wraps around the next letters

parts.note: home base is where one is based
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so Z

explanation.surface: A Republican base sheltering a lone unidentified gunman behind a shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' suggests guns; here it means plants sending up shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: This underground stem sends up new shoots, so it is where a plant's shoots come from.

clue.text: Amateur drama scores uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters of the joined words go

parts.note: a play is a piece of drama
scores of things means many of them

explanation.surface: An amateur dramatics production whose musical scores have been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' removes P and Y, the outer letters of PLAYMANY.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional, someone without expert training, is the plain counterpart to an expert.

clue.text: Audibly channel-hop in section of bar

indicators.note: audibly says we want what the words sound like spoken

parts.note: to graze is to flick idly through TV channels, so 'graze in'

explanation.surface: Flicking through TV channels while sitting in part of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAY'S INN is one of London's four Inns of Court, to one of which English barristers must belong before being called to the bar; 'bar' suggests a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar means the legal profession of barristers, divided among the Inns of Court, each a part of it.

clue.text: General hospital that's after no fee?

indicators.note: the hospital letter comes after the no-fee letters in the answer

parts.note: FOC stands for free of charge
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A general hospital that, seemingly, is only interested in patients who pay nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General hospital' reads as one phrase; split it, and 'General' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Foch was the French marshal who commanded the Allied armies in 1918.

clue.text: Dexter having to mark towards the goal?

parts.note: dexter, in heraldry, means on the right-hand side
to track is to trace or mark out a trail

explanation.surface: A man called Dexter gets to mark a player moving towards goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Dexter looks like a name; it is the Latin-derived word for right-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heading correctly towards an objective is making progress in the proper direction, as the idiom says.

clue.text: What makes use of strong guitar lead, say

definitions.text: What makes use of strong guitar
definitions.meaning: a loud rock genre built on distorted, powerful electric guitar
lead is an example of a dense toxic element of this class

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a guitar-driven rock genre and dense elements such as lead or mercury.

clue.text: Keep uncertain — half-heartedly confirm

parts.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle, a fort

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its doubled middle letter, and half of that is dropped

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or uncertain

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay in doubt and only give lukewarm agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the castle tower; 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two central Fs.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen a belief or resolve is to confirm it, as in being fortified in one's view.

clue.text: Tail cut off dog in old area around Whitefriars

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, which is docked here

parts.note: an Alsatian is the British name for a German shepherd dog

explanation.surface: A dog has had its tail docked in an old London district.
explanation.walkthrough: ALSATIA was the cant name for the lawless sanctuary district of Whitefriars in the City of London, where debtors hid.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the Whitefriars district off Fleet Street, a refuge for debtors and criminals, bore this nickname.

clue.text: Dry wine left by professional

indicators.note: left by means abandoned by, so the professional departs from the wine

parts.note: prosecco is an Italian sparkling wine
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A dry wine abandoned by a professional taster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry wine' reads as one phrase, but only 'Dry' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for dry, and also a technique of painting on dry plaster, versus fresco on wet.

clue.text: Singers taking exams in sweet devotion, shunning pressure

indicators.note: the exams are placed in the middle of the sweet

parts.note: a choc is a chocolate sweet
orals are spoken examinations

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so the pressure letter is left out

parts.note: piety is religious devotion
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Choristers sitting tests while lovingly devoted to sweets, but feeling no stress.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur choir is an organised group of vocalists, i.e. a body of singers.

clue.text: What might wipe out narrow connector in goggle

parts.note: a rubber is the British word for an eraser, which wipes out pencil marks
a neck is a narrow part joining head to body, or a bottle's spout

explanation.surface: Something that might erase a thin linking piece inside a pair of goggles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goggle' looks like a noun but is the verb: to stare.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawp nosily at something such as an accident is to stare, the verb sense of goggle.

clue.text: Virgin brides, unusually, put some of it about!

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the hidden letters round
only some of the letters of these words are used

explanation.surface: Untried brides, unusually, spread a little of 'it' around.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters DESUNU sit inside 'brides, unusually'; 'about' turns them round. 'unusually' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something virgin is fresh and untouched, never used before, as in virgin snow.

clue.text: Unruly daughter breaking image borne by prophet from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left
what is borne by something is carried within it, so the prophet holds the image

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest and prophet who taught Samuel

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the daughter splits the image

parts.note: an icon is a sacred image
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A wild daughter smashes a religious image carried by a prophet arriving from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' is the definition, not an anagram signal; 'from the east' reverses ELICODNI, the whole assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being not easily taught or managed is the opposite of docile, so it means unruly.

clue.text: Exemplify fashionable point of view

parts.note: in means in fashion
a stance is an opinion or position

explanation.surface: An instruction to illustrate a trendy opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite something as an example of a point is to give it as an illustration, the verb sense.

clue.text: Revealing jewellery worn by most of 70s group

indicators.note: here worn by sets the group's letters in the middle of the jewellery

parts.note: bling is flashy jewellery

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: ABBA were the Swedish pop group of the 1970s

explanation.surface: A picture of a seventies pop band showing off their flashy jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blurting a secret is giving it away, so the word means telling or disclosing.

clue.text: With machismo, save children

parts.note: save in the sense except is but

explanation.surface: A tough-guy instruction to rescue the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like rescue but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch describes a rugged, macho masculine manner, the swagger of machismo.

clue.text: University academic at first taken with joke book

parts.note: to josh is to joke or tease

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of academic is used

explanation.surface: A university academic, at first, is amused by a funny book.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshua is a book of the Old Testament, following Deuteronomy.

clue.text: Instrument for blowing through air-con with its front off

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone wrong or bad shows the letters are disordered

parts.note: the front of air-con is its first letter, A

explanation.surface: Something blown through an air-conditioning unit whose cover has come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front off' looks like a beheading, but 'off' is the anagram signal and 'with its front' adds A, the first letter of air-con.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, played by blowing into it.

clue.text: Empty bunker with continually rising echo

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards
an empty word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: ever means always or continually

explanation.surface: An empty bunker with an echo that keeps going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns BREVER upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An effect giving sound a lingering resonance, prolonging it like an echo.

clue.text: Act on suggestion of what bass may do?

definitions.meaning: to react to a provocation or tease as intended
a bass is a fish, which may come up to take an angler's lure

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for reacting to provocation, taken from a fish coming up to snap at a lure.

clue.text: The tiniest bit of salt mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so we want a word sounding like this

parts.note: salt, as in Attic salt, means sharp wit

explanation.surface: Talk of the smallest pinch of salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like seasoning but means keen humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest particle, as in 'not a whit', meaning not at all.

clue.text: Two presents returned after husband and wife swap novel

indicators.note: swap means the two letters change places
returned means the letters run backwards

parts.note: now and here are two words for the present time and place
H and W are abbreviations for husband and wife

explanation.surface: A tale of a couple exchanging two returned gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NOW HERE into EREHWON; then the H and W swap places. 'presents' suggests gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler's satirical Victorian novel is named after its imaginary land, nowhere spelt roughly backwards.

clue.text: Inscription of mine in middle of chapel following refurb

indicators.note: in places the mine inside the jumbled letters
following a refurbishment things are rearranged, so the middle letters are mixed up
middle of keeps all but the end letters of chapel

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: An inscription made by a miner sits in the middle of a newly refurbished chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following refurb' scrambles the chapel's middle letters into EAPH, which then takes the mine.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the commemorative writing carved on a tombstone.

clue.text: Patch of felt-like backing in skirt

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the hidden letters reverse
a patch is a piece of the material, so part of these letters is used

explanation.surface: A patch of feltlike lining in a skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: TLIK sits inside 'felt-like'; 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee-length pleated tartan skirt worn in Scottish dress.

clue.text: Spoiler alert — finally LBW with knee at crease

indicators.note: to crease is to crumple, so the letters are crumpled together
finally takes the last letter of alert

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: an LBW appeal as the batter's knee is struck while standing at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crease' looks like the cricket line; it is the anagram signal. LBW means leg before wicket, a way of being out in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy who dampens everyone's fun spoils things, the idiomatic damp blanket.
